method: The handicap per game is (base - average) x percentage / 100, rounded to the nearest whole pin with halves rounded up and never below zero, so an average at or above the base earns no pins. The average is limited to 0-300 pins and used exactly as entered, including a decimal; the base is limited to 100-300 pins, the percentage to 1-100 and the series to 1-10 games. The series handicap is the per-game figure multiplied by the number of games. When an opponent's average is entered, the same rule is applied to it, the difference between the two per-game handicaps is the match allowance, and entering both scratch series adds each series handicap to give the adjusted totals and the win, loss or tie. Negative (plus) handicaps, league maximums, average updates, no-tap or handicap-capped play and tournament allowances are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: United States Bowling Congress - league handicap rules: handicap = (base score - average) x handicap percentage
